subChunks.title: Responsive Design
subChunks.hookHtml: More than half your users are on a phone. A design that only works at 1440px wide isn't a design — it's an accident. Tailwind's breakpoint system enforces mobile-first discipline: you write for the smallest screen first, then layer on larger-screen enhancements.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
The mobile-first rule

In Tailwind, unprefixed utilities apply at all screen sizes. Breakpoint prefixes are minimum-width overrides — they activate at that width and above.

/* Mobile-first: base applies to all, breakpoints enhance */
class="text-base md:text-lg lg:text-xl"

/* text-base: mobile baseline (all sizes)
   md:text-lg: ≥768px override
   lg:text-xl: ≥1024px override */

The five breakpoints

sm:   ≥ 640px   — large phone / landscape
md:   ≥ 768px   — tablet
lg:   ≥ 1024px  — laptop
xl:   ≥ 1280px  — desktop
2xl:  ≥ 1536px  — large desktop

Responsive grid columns

/* 1 → 2 → 3 columns as screen grows */
class="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6"

Responsive flex direction

/* Stack on mobile, side-by-side on tablet+ */
class="flex flex-col md:flex-row gap-6"

Hiding and showing elements

hidden sm:block      /* hidden on mobile, visible from sm up */
block sm:hidden      /* visible on mobile, hidden from sm up */
hidden md:flex       /* hidden on mobile, flex from md up */

Responsive typography and spacing

/* Hero title — scales up */
class="text-3xl md:text-5xl lg:text-7xl font-bold"

/* Section padding — breathes more on large screens */
class="py-12 md:py-20 lg:py-32 px-4 md:px-8"

The container utility

/* Sets max-width + centres + adds horizontal padding */
class="container mx-auto px-4"

The common mistake — desktop-first undoing

/* WRONG — desktop-first, trying to undo for mobile */
class="grid-cols-3 sm:grid-cols-1"

/* RIGHT — mobile-first, progressively enhance */
class="grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3"

Tailwind breakpoints are min-width only. You cannot target "only below this size" without max-md: (which is a sign of inverted thinking). Always start with the mobile layout and add breakpoint prefixes to enhance upward.

Lyra: "The trap is writing the desktop layout first and trying to undo it for small screens. There is no way to say 'undo' — you can only add. So always start small. The unprefixed class is the mobile baseline. Every breakpoint prefix is an enhancement, not an override."

storyBeats.speaker: Lyra the Scribe
storyBeats.text: A spell that only works at the lectern is useless. Write for the smallest hand first. Then, with each breakpoint prefix, grant it larger ambitions.

storyBeats.speaker: Mobile-first responsive grid

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a responsive hero section that adapts from mobile to desktop:

  • .hero: py-16, md:py-24, lg:py-32, px-4, bg-slate-900
  • .hero-content: max-w-4xl, mx-auto, text-center
  • .hero-title: text-3xl, md:text-5xl, lg:text-7xl, font-bold, text-white, mb-6
  • .hero-subtitle: text-lg, md:text-xl, text-slate-400, mb-8, max-w-2xl, mx-auto
  • .hero-cta: inline-flex, items-center, gap-2, bg-blue-600, hover:bg-blue-700, text-white, px-6, md:px-8, py-3, md:py-4, rounded-lg, font-semibold, text-sm, md:text-base

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a responsive pricing card from scratch. On mobile it stacks vertically (plan name → price → feature list → CTA button). At the md breakpoint the card should increase its padding and the font sizes should scale up. No class list is given — choose appropriate utilities yourself.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain mobile-first in your own words. Why does Tailwind use min-width breakpoints rather than max-width? What goes wrong when developers write desktop-first CSS and try to override it for mobile? Explain the difference between hidden md:flex and flex md:hidden.

questions.prompt: At what minimum viewport width does the md: breakpoint activate in Tailwind's default configuration?
questions.explanation: Tailwind's default breakpoints: sm = 640px, md = 768px, lg = 1024px, xl = 1280px, 2xl = 1536px.

questions.prompt: You need cards to stack in a single column on mobile, show 2 columns on tablet, and 4 columns on desktop. Which class string is correct?
questions.explanation: Mobile-first: start with the single-column base (no prefix), then enhance at each breakpoint. The correct option uses unprefixed grid-cols-1 as the mobile baseline, md:grid-cols-2 for tablet, and lg:grid-cols-4 for desktop.

questions.prompt: A developer writes class="grid-cols-3 sm:grid-cols-2 xs:grid-cols-1" to make a grid that shows 1 column on very small screens. There are two bugs. What are they?
options: Bug 1: Tailwind has no xs: breakpoint — it's invalid. Bug 2: Logic is inverted (desktop-first) — grid-cols-3 applies to all sizes including mobile. Correct: grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3
Bug 1: sm: should be md: for tablets. Bug 2: xs: should be 2xs: for phones
Bug 1: Missing grid class. Bug 2: xs: is not supported — use max-sm: instead
Only one bug: xs: doesn't exist — the rest is fine
questions.answer: Bug 1: Tailwind has no xs: breakpoint — it's invalid. Bug 2: Logic is inverted (desktop-first) — grid-cols-3 applies to all sizes including mobile. Correct: grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3
questions.explanation: Tailwind's breakpoints start at sm (640px) — there is no xs. More importantly, because breakpoints are minimum-width, unprefixed utilities are the mobile baseline. grid-cols-3 without a prefix applies to all screen sizes, including mobile. The correct mobile-first pattern is grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3.
